title: A lighter for Dad
setting: Saturday afternoon at the family home. Yuki is back for the weekend and their dad's birthday is tomorrow. Kenji, half awake on the sofa, shows her the present he has bought.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: nee, mite. otousan no tanjoubi purezento, kore ni shita.
lines.ja: ねえ、見て。お父さんの誕生日プレゼント、これにした。
lines.kana: ねえ、みて。おとうさんのたんじょうびぷれぜんと、これにした。
lines.english: Hey, look. This is what I got Dad for his birthday.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, raitaa? kenji, shiranai no? otousan, sengetsu yameta n da yo.
lines.ja: え、ライター？ケンジ、知らないの？お父さん、先月やめたんだよ。
lines.kana: え、らいたー？けんじ、しらないの？おとうさん、せんげつやめたんだよ。
lines.english: Huh, a lighter? Kenji, didn't you know? Dad quit last month.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: やめた？え、会社やめたの？
lines.kana: やめた？え、かいしゃやめたの？
lines.english: Quit? Wait, he quit his job?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: chigau yo! tabako. tabako yameta no.
lines.ja: 違うよ！タバコ。タバコやめたの。
lines.kana: ちがうよ！たばこ。たばこやめたの。

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: maji de? anna ni tabako sutteta noni. nande?
lines.ja: マジで？あんなにタバコ吸ってたのに。なんで？
lines.kana: まじで？あんなにたばこすってたのに。なんで？
lines.english: Seriously? After all that smoking? How come?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mou toshi totta kara na tte. saikin, karada ni ii koto bakkari shiteru yo.
lines.ja: もう年取ったからなって。最近、体にいいことばっかりしてるよ。
lines.kana: もうとしとったからなって。さいきん、からだにいいことばっかりしてるよ。
lines.english: He says it's because he's getting old. Lately he's all about stuff that's good for him.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: aa, dakara asa, koohii ja nakute ocha nonderu n da.
lines.ja: ああ、だから朝、コーヒーじゃなくてお茶飲んでるんだ。
lines.kana: ああ、だからあさ、こーひーじゃなくておちゃのんでるんだ。
lines.english: Oh, so that's why he has tea in the morning now, not coffee.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou. ocha wa karada ni ii kara tte.
lines.ja: そう。お茶は体にいいからって。
lines.kana: そう。おちゃはからだにいいからって。
lines.english: Yep. He says tea's good for you.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: tabako yameta n nara, kore, mou tsukawanai yo ne. dou shiyou.
lines.ja: タバコやめたんなら、これ、もう使わないよね。どうしよう。
lines.kana: たばこやめたんなら、これ、もうつかわないよね。どうしよう。
lines.english: If he's quit smoking, he won't be using this anymore, will he? What do I do?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: karada ni ii mono ni shitara? toshi o toru to, sou iu no ga ureshii rashii yo.
lines.ja: 体にいいものにしたら？年を取ると、そういうのがうれしいらしいよ。
lines.kana: からだにいいものにしたら？としをとると、そういうのがうれしいらしいよ。
lines.english: Why not something that's good for him? Apparently that's what you like getting as you get older.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: jaa, soba wa? ii soba toka.
lines.ja: じゃあ、そばは？いいそばとか。
lines.kana: じゃあ、そばは？いいそばとか。
lines.english: Then how about soba? Some really good soba or something.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: soba wa dame. otousan, soba arerugii aru jan.
lines.ja: そばはダメ。お父さん、そばアレルギーあるじゃん。
lines.kana: そばはだめ。おとうさん、そばあれるぎーあるじゃん。
lines.english: Not soba. Dad's allergic to soba, remember?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: え、アレルギーあるの？知らなかった。
lines.kana: え、あれるぎーあるの？しらなかった。
lines.english: Wait, he has an allergy? I didn't know that.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mou, kenji wa otousan no koto, nanimo shiranai n da kara. tabako yameta no mo shiranakatta shi.
lines.ja: もう、ケンジはお父さんのこと、何も知らないんだから。タバコやめたのも知らなかったし。
lines.kana: もう、けんじはおとうさんのこと、なにもしらないんだから。たばこやめたのもしらなかったし。
lines.english: Honestly, Kenji, you don't know a thing about Dad. You didn't even know he'd quit smoking.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: gomen tte. jaa, ocha wa? ocha nara, arerugii nai yo ne?
lines.ja: ごめんって。じゃあ、お茶は？お茶なら、アレルギーないよね？
lines.kana: ごめんって。じゃあ、おちゃは？おちゃなら、あれるぎーないよね？
lines.english: All right, sorry! So what about tea? He's not allergic to tea, is he?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un, nai. ii ne, sore. kondo wa chanto kangaeta jan.
lines.ja: うん、ない。いいね、それ。今度はちゃんと考えたじゃん。
lines.kana: うん、ない。いいね、それ。こんどはちゃんとかんがえたじゃん。
lines.english: Nope, he isn't. That's a good one. You actually thought it through this time.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: aa, kangaetara tsukareta. toshi totta kana.
lines.ja: ああ、考えたら疲れた。年取ったかな。
lines.kana: ああ、かんがえたらつかれた。としとったかな。
lines.english: Ugh, all that thinking wore me out. Must be getting old.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: juunana de nani itten no. kinou osoku made okiteta dake desho.
lines.ja: 十七で何言ってんの。昨日遅くまで起きてただけでしょ。
lines.kana: じゅうななでなにいってんの。きのうおそくまでおきてただけでしょ。
lines.english: You're seventeen, what are you on about? You just stayed up too late last night.

choices.english: Kenji finds out his dad has quit his job, so they pick tea to cheer him up.
Kenji's lighter is no good as a present because his dad has quit smoking, so he picks tea instead.
Kenji wants to give his dad some good soba, and Yuki agrees because soba is good for you.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Kenji has bought his dad a lighter for his birthday. Lines 2-4: Yuki tells him their dad quit smoking last month (tabako yameta), and in line 9 Kenji sees the lighter is no use now. Soba is out because of an allergy (line 12), and in lines 15-16 they settle on tea. A is wrong: in line 3 Kenji thinks his dad quit his job (kaisha yameta), but Yuki corrects him straight away in line 4: it's smoking. C is wrong: Kenji does suggest soba (line 11), but Yuki says no, because their dad is allergic to it (line 12).

questions.english: You always drink tea, never coffee. Kenji asks you, "nande itsumo ocha na no? koohii no hou ga oishii jan." Tell him tea is good for you, using karada ni ii.
questions.ja: なんでいつもお茶なの？コーヒーのほうがおいしいじゃん。
questions.kana: なんでいつもおちゃなの？こーひーのほうがおいしいじゃん。
questions.romaji: nande itsumo ocha na no? koohii no hou ga oishii jan.
questions.answer: Say tea is good for you: ocha wa karada ni ii kara, keeping the ni even in casual speech. You could add that tea is better for you than coffee (ocha no hou ga karada ni ii).

modelAnswers.romaji: datte, ocha wa karada ni ii kara.
modelAnswers.ja: だって、お茶は体にいいから。

modelAnswers.romaji: koohii mo suki da kedo, ocha no hou ga karada ni ii n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: コーヒーも好きだけど、お茶のほうが体にいいんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: I like coffee too, but tea's better for you.

questions.explanation: In line 8 Yuki explains why their dad drinks tea now: ocha wa karada ni ii kara tte (because tea's good for you, he says), and lines 6 and 10 use karada ni ii for healthy habits and presents. It's said of food, drinks and habits, and ni stays even in casual talk. Don't say ocha wa kenkou desu: kenkou is a person's health, not something that's good for you. Kenji asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: At the end, Kenji says all that thinking has worn him out. What does he say next?
questions.ja: ケンジは最後に何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじはさいごになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa saigo ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: have I gone old and worn? (said of things)

questions.explanation: Line 17: toshi totta kana. People take on years, toshi o toru, and 'I'm getting old' comes out in the past (toshi totta), with o dropped in casual talk. Their dad's excuse in line 6 is the same phrase (mou toshi totta kara na), and Yuki uses the general form in line 10 (toshi o toru to, as you get older). A is wrong: furuku naru is for things wearing out, like old shoes, not people. B is wrong: toshi ga ue means older than someone, and Kenji isn't comparing himself with anyone.

questions.english: Kenji says, "tabako yameta n nara, kore, mou tsukawanai yo ne." What does he mean?
questions.ja: ケンジは何が言いたかったんですか？
questions.kana: けんじはなにがいいたかったんですか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa nani ga iitakatta n desu ka?

choices.english: His dad has given up smoking, so he won't have any use for the lighter now.
His dad smokes less these days, so he'll only use the lighter now and then.
His dad has left his job, so he won't need anything for the office.

questions.explanation: Line 9: tabako yameta means he has quit smoking. Yameru is giving up a habit for good, so Kenji adds mou tsukawanai (he won't use it anymore), meaning the lighter is no use as a present. B is wrong: yameta means he stopped completely, not that he cut down. C mixes it up with kaisha o yameru (quit your job), the same-sounding yameru Kenji wrongly jumped to in line 3. Yuki corrects him in line 4 (chigau yo! tabako).

questions.english: Like Kenji's dad, you're allergic to soba. Yuki asks you, "nee, ohiru, soba ni shinai?" Say you can't have it because of your allergy.
questions.ja: ねえ、お昼、そばにしない？
questions.kana: ねえ、おひる、そばにしない？
questions.answer: Say you have a soba allergy: soba arerugii aru (ga drops in casual talk), or soba no arerugii ga aru. Put the cause in front of arerugii, then suggest something else.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, gomen. soba arerugii aru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ごめん。そばアレルギーあるんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, sorry. I'm allergic to soba.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, watashi, soba no arerugii ga aru kara, hoka no ni shinai?
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、私、そばのアレルギーがあるから、ほかのにしない？
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've got a soba allergy, so can we have something else?

questions.explanation: An allergy is something you have, so it takes aru: Yuki says otousan, soba arerugii aru jan (line 12), Kenji echoes arerugii aru no? (line 13), and in line 15 he uses the negative, arerugii nai. The cause goes in front: soba arerugii, or soba no arerugii. Say it a-re-ru-gii, not like English 'allergy'. Yuki asks casually, so answer casually.
